title: Digital Twin Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Virtual representations of equipment, buildings, laboratories, and industrial systems. The Digital Twin Database documents virtual counterparts of physical things: equipment, buildings, labs, production lines — each twin mirroring its physical sibling's state, updated by live data, and usable for simulation, prediction, and training. A twin is not a 3D model (that is just visualization); it is a living model with physics, state synchronization, and a fidelity record stating exactly what it captures and what it does not.

title: Digital Twin Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Twin anatomy: physical asset <-> data link (sensors, update rate, latency) <-> virtual model (geometry + physics + state) <-> services (dashboards, predictions, simulations). Model types: physics-based (equations, interpretable, needs parameters), data-driven (ML on historical data, needs coverage), hybrid (physics + learned corrections — usually best). Synchronization: real-time (control), near-real-time (monitoring), periodic (planning); latency budget per use case. Fidelity: validate twin predictions against asset measurements; record error bands; re-validate after asset changes. Use cases: monitoring (current state), prediction (remaining useful life), what-if (simulate changes safely), training (operators practice on the twin). Lifecycle: version the twin with the asset; decommissioning is a record too.

demo.title: Execution: A* pathfinding on a grid
demo.code: const grid=[[0,0,0,1],[0,1,0,0],[0,0,0,0]];const W=4,H=3;function h(a,b){return Math.abs(a[0]-b[0])+Math.abs(a[1]-b[1]);}function astar(s,g){const open=[{p:s,f:h(s,g),c:0}],came={},cost={[s]:0};while(open.length){open.sort((a,b)=>a.f-b.f);const cur=open.shift();if(cur.p[0]===g[0]&&cur.p[1]===g[1]){const path=[g];let k=g+'';while(came[k]){path.unshift(came[k]);k=came[k]+'';}return path;}for(const [dx,dy] of [[1,0],[-1,0],[0,1],[0,-1]]){const n=[cur.p[0]+dx,cur.p[1]+dy];if(n[0]<0||n[1]<0||n[0]>=H||n[1]>=W||grid[n[0]][n[1]])continue;const nc=cur.c+1;if(cost[n+'']===undefined||nc<cost[n+'']){cost[n+'']=nc;came[n+'']=cur.p;open.push({p:n,f:nc+h(n,g),c:nc});}}}}const path=astar([0,0],[2,3]);J({steps:path.length-1});assert(path.length-1===5,'astar');

title: Digital Twin Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Tests: fidelity test (predictions within stated bands); sync test (data freshness meets the budget); fitness test (use cases matched to validated capabilities); determinism test. Limitations: demos use sample data; real twins need instrumented assets; fidelity degrades without re-validation (schedule in the record). Every twin carries its fidelity statement and validation log.

demo.title: Execution: Hohmann transfer delta-v
demo.code: const mu=398600;function circ(r){return Math.sqrt(mu/r);}const r1=6678,r2=42164;const a=(r1+r2)/2;const dv1=Math.abs(Math.sqrt(mu*(2/r1-1/a))-circ(r1));const dv2=Math.abs(circ(r2)-Math.sqrt(mu*(2/r2-1/a)));J({dv1:+dv1.toFixed(2),dv2:+dv2.toFixed(2),total:+(dv1+dv2).toFixed(2)});assert(dv1+dv2>3.8&&dv1+dv2<4.0,'hohmann');
